headline: Record-Breaking US Heat Dome Engulfs 70 Million as Third Heat Emergency of the Month Spans 20+ States
overview: A catastrophically broad heat dome — the third in a single month — now places roughly 70 million Americans under dangerous heat conditions, with heat indices reaching 116°F in Missouri and Kansas and air temperatures up to 118°F in Phoenix and 120°F in Death Valley. Separately, deadly flash floods struck eastern Afghanistan (at least 26 dead) and West Virginia (at least 2 dead, search and rescue ongoing), while multiple large wildfires continue to burn across southern Europe and the US boundary waters region. The scale and simultaneity of extreme events across multiple continents make this an exceptionally active natural hazard day.

events.title: Third US Heat Dome of July Engulfs 70 Million — Heat Index Hits 116°F Across 20+ States
events.location: Missouri, Kansas, Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Arkansas, Tennessee, Mississippi, Arizona, California, and more — USA
events.summary: An expansive and intensifying heat dome — the third to strike the central and southern US in a single month — now covers more than 20 states and threatens roughly 70 million people with dangerously hot conditions. Active Extreme Heat Warnings span from the Coachella Valley and Phoenix metro (110–118°F) through the central plains (heat indices of 108–116°F in Missouri and Kansas) to Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, Arkansas, Tennessee, and Mississippi. With little overnight temperature relief and no immediate end in sight through Monday, heat-related illness risk is at its highest level of the season.

events.title: Afghanistan Flash Floods Kill at Least 26 in Eastern Provinces
events.summary: Devastating flash floods swept through eastern Afghanistan — particularly the mountainous Nuristan province — killing at least 26 people and leaving scores missing, according to UN agencies and rescue workers on the scene. Buildings were destroyed and rescue teams faced extreme difficulty accessing remote flood-affected communities due to damaged roads and infrastructure. Aid agencies are racing to deliver emergency assistance as search operations continue in the rubble.

events.title: West Virginia Catastrophic Flash Flooding — 2 Dead, Search and Rescue Ongoing
events.summary: Catastrophic flash flooding struck north-central West Virginia after powerful storms dropped more than 7 inches of rain in a short period, prompting a rare Flash Flood Emergency declaration from the National Weather Service. At least two people have been confirmed dead, with the state government placing the response in a search-and-rescue phase as floodwaters covered roads including Interstate 79. A state of emergency was declared as crews continued to look for additional victims.

events.title: Spain Wildfire National Emergency — 60,000 Evacuated from Madrid and Ávila Suburbs
events.location: Madrid, Ávila, and Guadalajara Province, Spain
events.summary: Spain has declared a national emergency as wildfires burning west of Madrid and into the Ávila province forced the evacuation of approximately 60,000 residents from towns and suburbs in the region. Blazes have consumed large swaths of dry vegetation amid a prolonged European heat wave and drought, overwhelming local firefighting resources. The national emergency declaration allows for coordinated military and federal firefighting assets to be deployed across the affected provinces.

events.title: France Gironde Wildfire — Cap Ferret Peninsula Fully Evacuated by Boat
events.location: Cap Ferret Peninsula, Gironde, Southwestern France
events.summary: French authorities have ordered and completed the total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula — a major tourist destination near Bordeaux — deploying boats to move residents and visitors cut off by fire-damaged roads as wildfires continue to rage through the Gironde department. Firefighters from across France and neighboring EU countries are battling the blazes amid drought conditions and high winds. France has formally requested EU civil protection assistance, with President Macron directly overseeing the national response.

events.title: Boundary Waters and Superior National Forest Fires — 63,000+ Acres, Pyrocumulonimbus Clouds Observed
events.location: Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness, Northern Minnesota, USA
events.summary: More than a dozen active wildfires are burning across the Boundary Waters Canoe Area (BWCA) and Superior National Forest in northern Minnesota, with combined acreage exceeding 63,000 acres as of mid-week and growing. The fires — ignited by lightning — have grown intense enough to generate pyrocumulonimbus (fire-generated thunderstorm) clouds, a hallmark of the most extreme wildfire behavior, as documented by NASA satellite imagery. Smoke from these fires is contributing to widespread air quality degradation across the Upper Midwest.

events.title: Death Valley and Southwest Desert Extreme Heat Peaks — Up to 120°F, Warnings Extended Through Monday
events.location: Death Valley, Coachella Valley, Phoenix Metro, Colorado River Valley — Arizona, California, Nevada, USA
events.summary: Extreme Heat Warnings across the Desert Southwest remain in force through Monday evening as temperatures in Death Valley and along the Colorado River Valley are forecast to reach or exceed 120°F — among the highest reliably recorded temperatures on Earth. Phoenix is under warning for 110–118°F afternoon highs with overnight lows above 80°F providing negligible relief, and the Coachella Valley is seeing highs of 110–116°F. NWS Las Vegas classified heat risk at the extreme (purple) HeatRisk level, its highest category, for the greater Mojave Desert region.
